          Liverpool vs Man City: Six Key Subplots Ahead of Sunday’s Charged Anfield Encounter
        
      
                          
                      Oct 10, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Reem Sarraf / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
All eyes will be on Anfield this Sunday when Liverpool host Manchester City in the Premier League. Leading into the game, we identify the key narratives to look out for.
Sunday’s clash between Liverpool and Manchester City is one of the most fascinating Premier League matches for years.
While there will be the usual intrigue of a heavyweight duel, the heat for this one has been dialled up by off-field matters that developed significantly during the international break.

On 29 September, the Premier League confirmed an independent commission found “Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation”.

City deny the allegations and confirmed on 2 October they had lodged an appeal, with any potential sanctions still to be determined. Nevertheless, it was a seismic development and one that could have a monumental impact on English football.
Sunday’s game will be City’s first outing since, and they can look forward to an especially vociferous welcome to Anfield.
Ahead of the match, we’ve identified several aspects that might gives clues as to which way the game goes – and there’s only one place to start…

Given what happened during the international break, City would’ve been expecting a hostile reception wherever they were playing next. But if they could’ve picked any ground not to play their first match following the guilty verdicts, Anfield – if not Old Trafford – would probably be the one.
For starters, there are few top-flight grounds in England as hostile as Anfield when the home fans are in the mood. And you can guarantee they’ll be up for this one.
But on top of that, City, like so many others, have a dreadful record at Anfield even at the best of times.

Of grounds they have played at more than once in the Premier League, they only have a worse points-per-game rate at Highbury (0.22) than they do at Anfield (0.59), and they have played more than three times as many games at the latter (29) as they have at Arsenal’s former home (nine).

In total, City have won only three of their 29 Premier League trips to Anfield, giving them one of their worst win rates (10.3%) at any stadium. They have also lost 18 of those games, equating to a 62.1% loss rate at Liverpool.

City did win there last season, coming from behind with two late goals to snatch a 2-1 win, but that came when Liverpool were in a particularly difficult moment that saw them manage one win in seven games, their title defence crumbling.
There was also a City win at Anfield in February 2021, though that was when games were played with no fans present due to the COVID-19 pandemic. That was their first win there in 18 visits.

Anfield is simply a very tough place to go. Even though Liverpool haven’t been the outright best side for much of the Premier League era, away sides still have a lower win percentage at Anfield (12.5%) than at any other stadium.
City will at least be going into the match in decent form.
After five matches, City are top of the Premier League having won all their matches, including a 1-0 victory at Manchester United in the derby despite spending over an hour with 10 men.

However, it is a little difficult to know how much City’s start will count for because, well, these are uncharted waters. Firstly, we’ve just had an unprecedented three-week international break, and secondly, we’ve no idea to what degree the off-field matters will have distracted Enzo Maresca’s team.
City’s situation might stoke something of a siege mentality in the squad, or it might overwhelm them.
Either way, despite obviously making a good start to the season (on the pitch), City haven’t looked unbeatable and can certainly consider themselves fortunate to have 15 points.
